Result Report BHARTI reported consol. Revenue and EBITDA of INR608.8bn and INR349.5bn inline with est. up 4.0% and 4.9% QoQ respectively, driven by strong momentum across India and Africa operations. In India Mobile, ARPU of INR271 came inline with our est (PLe: INR269), although subscriber additions of 0.7mn remained below our expectation (PLe: 4.0mn). Performance across the Home and Enterprise businesses remained steady, with EBITDA growing 1.4% and 1.3% QoQ, respectively. Homes continued to report healthy subscriber additions of 0.7mn; however, ARPU declined 2.6% QoQ to INR509. Digital business remained subdued, with EBITDA flat QoQ declining 8.8% YoY due to weakness in DTH business. Africa continued to deliver resilient performance with EBITDA margins growing to 50.3% vs 49.3% QoQ. Management remains focused on driving ARPU growth through pricing interventions and customer premiumization. In Homes, BHARTI is prioritizing FTTH expansion while scaling back FWA-led expansion. Africa continues as a long-term growth opportunity. Maintain BUY with a revised TP of INR2,411 (earlier INR2,367), based on an implied 12.2x Sep’28 EV/EBITDA for the India business, while additionally incorporating the value of investments in Airtel Africa, Indus Towers and Bharti Hexacom. India Mobile business remained strong: Revenue increased 3.4% QoQ and 10.1% YoY to INR309.4bn, while EBITDA grew 3.8% QoQ and 11.3% YoY to INR188.8bn, supported by ARPU expansion of 2.7% QoQ / 5.9% YoY to INR271 partly benefiting from 1 additional day in the quarter. However, subscriber additions remained weak at 0.7mn compared to 3.3mn in Q1FY27, while postpaid business recorded its highest-ever quarterly net additions of 1.2mn, taking the postpaid customer base to 31.2mn, EBITDA margins increased to 61.0% vs 60.8% QoQ. Monthly churn increased to 2.9% vs 2.6% QoQ due to seasonality and the prepaid pricing intervention, resulting in an impact on customer retention. BHARTI expects sustained ARPU expansion through plan upgrades, postpaid conversions, international roaming and top-ups. Factoring in these trends, we estimate BHARTI's subscriber base at 381/389/395mn in FY27/FY28/29E, marginally lowering our FY27/FY28E estimates from 386/394mn, respectively, following lower than expected subscriber additions in Q2FY27. We raise our ARPU estimates to INR275/302/311 for FY27/28/29E, respectively, from INR272/290 for FY27/28E, factoring in the benefits of pricing interventions, continued customer premiumization and anticipated Tariff hike. EBITDA margins declined to 48.8% vs 49.1% QoQ. Customer additions improved to 0.7mn from 0.5mn in Q1FY27, although ARPU declined 4.2%/2.6% YoY/QoQ to INR509. The ARPU moderation primarily reflects management's correction of low-ARPU customer acquisitions. As per BHARTI, demand remains concentrated in the top 1,000 cities. Company’s focus will be on accelerating FTTH expansion, while scaling back FWA-led expansion as a structural strategic shift. FWA will primarily serve as an interim solution to capture demand until fibre connectivity is deployed in a particular area Digital Business remains a drag: Revenue grew 2.4% YoY but remained flat QoQ to INR7.7bn. EBITDA declined 8.8% YoY, while remaining flat QoQ at INR3.3bn. EBITDA margins remained steady at 43.3% vs 2.9% QoQ.
